# File ownership by an embedded alef marker

## Context and Problem Statement

alef writes two kinds of files into a consumer repository: outputs it regenerates on every run, and starter files
(manifests, READMEs, sample tests) that a person is expected to edit afterwards. It needs a rule for which files it
owns and may rewrite, and a way to tell when an owned file has gone stale. The way it checks staleness has changed
three times:

* Until 0.8.3, `alef verify` diffed each generated file's on-disk content against a fresh render, so an external
  formatter run over the output (php-cs-fixer, rubocop, ruff, biome) produced false drift.
* 0.8.3 (748b905d4, 2026-04-26) made verify "a pure hash comparison" against an embedded `alef:hash:` line, and
  stated the ownership rule: "Files without an alef hash header ... are skipped — alef has no claim over them."
* By 5dec17920 (2026-08-27) the embedded hash had become a content-only stamp: a blake3 of the file's own bytes,
  which detects a hand-edit and nothing else.
* 683fe82ec and d48c3326f (2026-09-26) added a fresh-render diff back: verify renders each owned file, runs the
  formatter alef itself would run, and compares the result with the bytes on disk. The commit records the
  reason: a content-only stamp "catches a hand-edit but never a file that is internally self-consistent and stale".

## Considered Options

* Ownership by an alef marker in the file's header, with unmarked files treated as create-once seeds and the
  `alef:hash:` line as a hand-edit stamp
* Diff each generated file's on-disk content against a raw fresh render (before 0.8.3)
* Verify by the embedded hash alone (0.8.3 to 2026-09-26)

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "Ownership by an alef marker in the file's header, with unmarked files treated as create-once seeds and
the `alef:hash:` line as a hand-edit stamp", because 0.8.3 made the header the claim: a file without it is one
"alef has no claim over". Of the three verify designs, only this ownership rule has survived every change.

* 3f8497139 (2026-08-14) made the marker itself the test: every file whose content carries an alef marker is
  stamped and verified, and `generated_header` only says whether a header is prepended. The marker is searched for
  only in the first 10 lines of a file (`MARKER_SCAN_LINES`).
* Unmarked files alef creates are create-once seeds: written only when absent, then user-owned. 86b1a7f16
  (2026-08-17) made `alef adopt` refuse them, and 779f7ba18 (2026-08-18) split overwriting them off `--clean`; both
  now need `--clobber-create-once-seeds`.
* Staleness of an owned file is decided by the fresh-render diff, and the `alef:hash:` stamp detects a hand-edit.

### Consequences

* Good, because a hand-grown manifest or test suite is never overwritten by a regeneration.
* Good, because a hand-edit to an owned file is detected even when the generation inputs did not change.
* Bad, because a create-once seed whose content goes stale is never updated by alef. `alef verify` reports it as
  "frozen path(s) DRIFTED" without failing, and the consumer must fix it by hand.
* Bad, because ownership hangs on a marker phrase ("generated by alef") in the first 10 lines, so a hand-written file
  that contains it there, without a negation such as "not", is claimed, and a marker placed lower is missed.

### Confirmation

* `src/core/hash.rs:31` documents `alef:hash:` as "a pure function of the file's own content" that answers whether
  the file was hand-edited.
* `src/core/hash/markers.rs:11` defines the shared marker substring, `src/core/hash.rs:297` the
  `content_has_alef_marker` test, and `src/core/hash.rs:326` sets `MARKER_SCAN_LINES` to 10.
* `src/bin_cli/helpers/format_drift.rs:1` documents the fresh-render drift comparison.
* `src/cli/pipeline/generate/scaffold.rs:225` documents scaffold files as create-only by default, and
  `src/bin_cli/args.rs:315` declares `--clobber-create-once-seeds`.
